Very faint, narrow (<10 degree half-width), jet-like CME first seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 starting at 2026-08-02T10:45Z. In real time, this CME was only seen in GOES CCOR-1. The source is most likely a small piece of ejecta seen over the NE limb in SDO AIA 304 starting at 2026-08-02T09:09Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to single view point and beyond-limb source.

data.note: CME observed best to the E in STEREO A COR2. Also observed faintly to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 until a downlink gap begins at 2026-08-03T05:00Z, and faintly to the W in GOES CCOR-1. The source may be gradual field line brightening/opening from AR 14501 (S07W43) lasting from approximately 2026-08-03T00:00Z to 2026-08-03T04:00Z in SDO AIA 193/211. The CME is likely deflected northeastward with proximity to the large southern polar coronal hole seen facing STEREO A EUVI.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2, and GOES CCOR-1. The front is notably more faint in LASCO and CCOR-1.

data.note: CME observed to the NE in only STEREO A COR2, likely obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The CME is unavailable in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 real-time due to a downlink gap. The likely source is AR 14498, observed in SDO AIA 304 first as a filament liftoff with surface brightening starting around 2026-08-03T07:10Z, followed by a wider swath of faint dimming and brightening starting around 2026-08-03T08:16Z in SDO AIA 171/193, all centered ~N22W12.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only 3D analysis using N22W12 as the approximate source, finding some northward deflection. May be some variance in the parameters without other coronagraph imagery to triangulate.

data.note: CME observed to the SE in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is a filament eruption on the south central disk centered around S35W05. The filament in SDO AIA 304 begins to lift as early as approximately 2026-08-03T03:00Z, with most of the eruption seen from 2026-08-03T07:00Z to 2026-08-03T12:00Z, with brightening on-disk. This CME is also observed in SDO AIA 193 as a wide swath of dimming starting at approximately 2026-08-03T10:00Z which migrates southeastward for several hours and covers a large area of the south-central disk. The filament eruption, field line movement, dimming, and brightening are also seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304 at 2026-08-03T07:55Z and 2026-08-03T08:15Z respectively.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery in real-time. The source may be a far-sided filament eruption beyond the NE limb as best seen in GOES SUVI 284/304 imagery at 2026-08-04T06:29Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: This is a plane of sky measurement using STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: CME first seen to the SE in STEREO A COR2. The CME is also seen in GOES CCOR-1 starting around 2026-08-04T14:00Z. The potential source is not clear, but may be a faint region of dimming seen in the SE of SDO AIA 193 imagery, centered around S40E30, between 2026-08-04T06:00Z-09:00Z. Moving/opening field lines are also visible off the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA, GOES SUVI 284, and STEREO A EUV 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential estimated source location.

data.note: CME visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and the NW in GOES CCOR-1. Not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a data gap. The source is likely an eruption from approximately N25W30 with dimming, moving field lines, and post-eruptive arcades best seen in SDO AIA 193 and STEREO A EUV 195 starting around 2026-08-04T12:25Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement based on the source location as well as the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Preliminary measurement based on approximate source location using STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: CME first seen to the NE by GOES CCOR-1 beginning at 2026-08-04T20:15Z. This CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-04T06:24Z and is not seen in STEREO A COR2 in real time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-04T19:09Z. The source of this event is field line movement/opening seen in SDO AIA 171 from beyond the Northeast limb beginning at approx. 2026-08-04T19:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using a longitude of E90 due to source beyond the E limb and lack of STEREO A COR2 to triangulate.

data.note: Narrow CME first seen to the NNW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-08-04T22:00Z. This event is only visible in C2 as it is obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and is not visible in STEREO A COR2 in real time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-04T19:09Z. The source of this CME is likely far sided beyond the NW limb, but faint field line movement can be seen in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-08-04T21:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using a longitude of W90 due to source from beyond the NW limb and lack of STEREO A imagery to triangulate.

data.note: CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-08-04T23:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. This event is not visible in STEREO A COR2 in real time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-04T19:09Z. The source of this CME is a filament eruption seen from just beyond the NE limb in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304 beginning at 2026-08-04T22:55Z along with field line opening visible in SDO AIA 171, 193 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement using limited early frames of SOHO LASCO C2 imagery.

data.note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-08-05T01:26Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the N in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely a secondary filament eruption following the filament eruption that caused CME: 2026-08-04T23:48Z. This second filament eruption is best seen in SDO AIA 304 over the NE limb beginning around 2026-08-05T00:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 starting around 2026-08-05T08:15Z. In real time, this CME is covered by data gaps between downlinks for SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, which later backfilled. The source of this CME is likely an eruption centered around N10E40-50 beginning as early as 2026-08-05T05:30Z. Some filamentary ejecta can been seen in SDO AIA 304 as well as a minor EUV wave followed by an area of dimming in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement based on additional available SOHO LASCO C3 imagery.
Very speculative, preliminary single coronagraph measurement based on source location.

data.note: CME visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 imagery and the NNE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is visible in SOHO LASCO C3 at 2026-08-05T18:42Z after a downlink data gap but is out of the field of view in SOHO LASCO C2 in real-time. The source may be an eruption with moving field lines beyond the NE limb best seen in GOES SUVI 284 imagery starting at 2026-08-05T11:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential source location.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the N in STEREO A COR2 starting around 2026-08-06T00:53Z. It is also partially seen to the NNE in GOES CCOR-1 around the pylon but is covered by a real time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source may be related to some minor field line movement seen beyond the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-08-06T00:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the ENE in GOES CCOR-1 beginning as early as 2026-08-06T03:00Z. The start time is somewhat subjective because the early rise off the solar disk is very slow. This feature is only seen in GOES CCOR-1. The source may be related to some faint field line movement near the E limb best seen in SDO AIA 171 beginning as early as 2026-08-05T23:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative plane-of-sky measurement based only on later frames of GOES CCOR-1. The early propagation of the CME is obscured by Earth-shine.

data.note: Very faint, narrow CME first seen to the NE is GOES CCOR-1. The feature is only seen in GOES CCOR-1 in real time. The source may be related to a very small piece of ejecta seen on the E limb in SDO AIA 304 beginning around 2026-08-06T08:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to single coronagraph view and on-limb source.

data.note: This CME is visible to the W/SW in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source of this CME is a filament eruption visible to the SW in STEREO A EUVI 304 around 2026-08-06T16:15Z with associated moving/opening field lines, dimming, and brightening visible to the SW in STEREO A EUVI 195. The source is in close proximity to an equatorial coronal hole.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is no SOHO imagery available currently due to an on going data gap. There was likely deflection within the field of view due to proximity of a coronal hole.

data.note: CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-08-07T06:36Z. It is also seen to the E in GOES CCOR-1 and to the NE in STEREO A COR2. Only the earliest frames of SOHO LASCO C2 are seen in real time. Most of the propagation of the CME is covered by a real-time data gap between downlink periods in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source of this CME is most likely an eruption just beyond the E limb best seen in GOES SUVI 284 as opening field lines beginning around 2026-08-07T05:37Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Narrow and semi-bright outflow like CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and GOES CCOR-1. There is a data gap for this event in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be moving/opening field lines visible beyond the NE limb in SDO/AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-08-07T21:00Z, however it is not the best timing for the visible features in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and GOES CCOR-1.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 frames. The feature appears to deflect further north as it travels through the field of view which may have impacted the fit and initial measurement of this CME.

data.note: CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and faintly to the N in STEREO A COR2. This is the second in a quick series of fronts to the NE at 2026-08-07T21:00Z, 2026-08-08T23:00Z, and 2026-08-08T00:36Z. The source is lengthy continuous field line movement over the E limb in SDO AIA 171 as early as 2026-08-07T20:12Z, and the field line movement likely responsible for this CME can be seen starting around 2026-08-07T21:03Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. This front is quite faint in COR2, but more visibly northward than the brighter, NE CME: 2026-08-08T00:36Z.

data.note: CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. This is the third in a quick series of fronts to the NE at 2026-08-07T21:00Z, 2026-08-08T23:00Z, and 2026-08-08T00:36Z. The source is lengthy continuous field line movement over the E limb in SDO AIA 171 as early as 2026-08-07T20:12Z, and the field line movement likely responsible for this CME can be seen starting around 2026-08-07T23:03Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2, noting the fit appears deflected westward to ~E74 from the observed SDO source likely on/just beyond the E limb.

data.note: CME observed to the N/NW in SOHO LASCO C2 and not yet in LASCO C3 before a DSN gap begins at 2026-08-08T05:00Z. The CME is visible to the N/NW in GOES CCOR-1 but heavily obscured by the pylon. The CME is best seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The source is a filament eruption on the north central disk; the full eruption spans approximately N28E35 to N08W00, centered ~N20E10 in SDO AIA 193. The eruption is observed as filament ejecta and double ribbon flare in SDO AIA 304 first lifting around 2026-08-08T00:48Z and fully erupting at 2026-08-08T02:10Z. The CME is also seen as a prominence on the NE limb of STEREO A EUVI 195/304. Dimming, field line movement, and post eruptive arcades are observed in SDO AIA 171/193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and 4 available frames of SOHO LASCO C2 due to the DSN data gap, and the GOES CCOR-1 pylon too heavily obscuring the leading edge to reliably track with.

data.note: Filament eruption CME observed to the SW in GOES CCOR-1 and as a SE halo in STEREO A COR2. Not observed in real-time in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to DSN gap starting 2026-08-08T05:00Z. The source is a long-spanning filament eruption from the SW disk, with eastward deflection observed best from STEREO A's perspective. The eruption starts around 2026-08-08T05:37Z, observed in SDO AIA 171/193/211/304 and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 as filament ejecta, double ribbon flare and brightening, field line movement, minimal dimming, and a post-eruptive arcade. The eruption spans approximately ~S20W40 to ~S15W90 (centered S17W65).

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1, noting the eastward deflection from the observed source longitude as seen in STEREO A EUVI 304. This analysis captures the bulk of the bright LE material in both spacecraft.

data.note: CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-08-08T16:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a small amount of field line opening seen in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-08-08T15:00Z located at approx. S15W55.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint, wide, slow CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the SW in STEREO A COR2. The source is clearly far-sided via CME triangulation, and may only be observed in GOES SUVI 284 as slow moving field lines over the SE limb starting as early as 2026-08-08T15:00Z the previous day; noting this observation as more speculative.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely on or very near the NE limb, observed as a filament eruption and field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193/304 starting around 2026-08-09T02:52Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on triangulation between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Narrow CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. Not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source can be seen as moving field lines beyond the NE limb best seen in SDO AIA 193 imagery starting around 2026-08-09T22:24Z. This eruption may be associated with an active region around N10E105 seen in Solar Orbiter EUI 174 imagery at 2026-08-09T12:06Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on potential source location.

data.note: CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is visible in SOHO LASCO C2 until 2026-08-10T07:00Z and is not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 in real-time due to a data gap in the DSN. The source may be an eruption seen near N10W130 in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery starting at 2026-08-10T01:25Z as brightening and moving field lines.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source location as well as the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. The source is an eruption and C2.4 flare starting around 2026-08-10T12:30Z from former Active Region 14498, which was located at an approximate longitude of 102 degrees around the time of the eruption, as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the western limb in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195/284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the longitude of former Active Region 14498 based on the approximate rate of solar rotation.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 only, either too faint or blocked by the pylon in LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely far-sided, observed only in SDO AIA 171 as field line movement over the NNW limb around 2026-08-11T12:43Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

data.note: CME first seen to the NW by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-08-012T08:23Z, as well as to the North by GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not seen in SOHO LASCO in real-time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-12T04:35Z. The source of this event is likely far sided, and is seen as field lines opening along or just beyond the West limb (approx. N15W157) in STEREO A EUVI 195 and from beyond the North limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-08-23T07:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME first seen to the East in STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-08-14T05:09Z, as well as by GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME was not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-14T04:48Z. The source of this event is a filament eruption centered at approx. S10E20 with liftoff beginning at approx. 2026-08-14T04:00Z. This filament is heavily deflected to the West as it erupts as seen in SDO AIA, STEREO A EUVI and GOES SUVI 304. Field line opening, dimming and post eruptive arcades are also visible in SDO AIA 171, 193, STEREO A EUVI 195 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME first seen as a halo to the SE by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-08-14T07:38Z, as well as by GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME was not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-14T04:48Z. The source of this event is a C4.1 flare from Active Region 14503 (S17W57) seen peaking at 2026-08-14T07:01Z in SDO AIA 131. Field line opening, dimming and post eruptive arcades are also visible in SDO AIA 94, 171, 193, STEREO A EUVI 195 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME observed to the W in STEREO A COR2 and as a NE partial halo in GOES CCOR-1, not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to DSN gap, but imagery became available with later backfill. The source is far-sided, only likely visible as field line movement over the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 starting as early as 2026-08-14T10:42Z and over the NE limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting around 2026-08-14T10:55Z. This CME is preceded by a faint front that is quickly overtaken by the main bulk of this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: UPDATED BULK measurement based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
SHOCK measurement based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
PRELIMINARY measurement based on triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME first seen to the W in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-08-14T18:23Z. It is also seen to the W in GOES CCOR-1. In real time, this CME is covered by a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source of this CME is most likely related to moving field lines seen beyond the W limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-08-14T17:18Z. An eruption that may be related can been seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 near former AR 14505 (located approximately N15W145) beginning around 2026-08-14T16:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME first seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-08-14T22:24Z. It is also seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C3 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The majority of the CME is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. A possible source is a small filament eruption beyond the N limb best seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2026-08-14T21:52Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: This flare originated from former Active Region 14498 which rotated off of the Earth-facing disk on 2026-08-09.
